name: Indolent Primary Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma
aliases: Primary Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma, Indolent Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of persistent, slowly progressive cutaneous patches or plaques without systemic involvement
Skin biopsy showing epidermotropic atypical T-cell infiltrate with cerebriform nuclei
T-cell markers positive (CD3+, CD4+), loss of pan-T-cell antigens (e.g., CD7), and monoclonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement
Absence of extracutaneous disease confirmed by imaging and laboratory studies
Indolent clinical course with slow progression over years

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria including clinical presentation, histopathology, immunophenotyping, and exclusion of systemic involvement must be met.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, histological, and molecular findings to exclude aggressive lymphoma variants.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent erythematous patches or plaques with fine scaling
searchTerms: long-lasting red skin areas with scaling

pathognomonic.symptomName: Epidermotropism of atypical cerebriform T-lymphocytes on skin biopsy
searchTerms: atypical immune cells in skin sample

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas
Hypopigmented or hyperpigmented macules or patches
Slowly enlarging cutaneous lesions over months to years

occasional.symptomName: Secondary skin infections in affected areas
Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever

occasional.symptomName: Eczematous changes or scaling resembling dermatitis

rare.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (weight loss, night sweats)
searchTerms: systemic symptoms like chills and weight loss
B symptoms including sweating and fever

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear typically normal or minimal atypical lymphocytes
T-cell receptor gene rearrangement monoclonality detected by PCR
imaging: CT or PET scans show no extracutaneous lymphadenopathy or organ involvement
genetic: No recurrent chromosomal translocations typical for aggressive lymphomas
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating epidermotropism and Pautrier microabscesses
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD3, CD4; loss of CD7

distinguishingFeatures: Histology shows parakeratosis and neutrophilic infiltrates

redFlags: Development of systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, night sweats)
Appearance of nodules or tumors on skin
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.
Kim YH, Willemze R, Pimpinelli N, et al. TNM classification system for primary cutaneous lymphomas other than mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome. Blood. 2007;110(2):479-484.
